Acceptance checks of a calibration

Source: R/calibration_checks.R
calibration_checks.Rd

A calibration can score well over the whole record and still be wrong where it matters. NSE over a long record weighs time steps, not events, so a model whose flood peaks are late and low can score 0.9 when its recessions are right. These checks look for two warning signs the headline score hides.

Usage

calibration_checks(
  project,
  entry = NULL,
  top = 20L,
  edge = 0.01,
  rain_min = NULL,
  max_response_h = 150,
  screen = list()
)

Arguments

project

A calibration project folder.

entry

Id of a model entry (structure, trial or calibration) or candidate; by default the latest candidate.

top

Largest events summarised in each window.

edge

Distance from a bound, as a share of the searched range, within which a parameter counts as at the bound.

rain_min, max_response_h

Passed to find_events().

screen

Settings for screen_events(), with the project's highest gauged flow unless they name one; NULL summarises every event.

Value

A pdm_calibration_checks list of three data frames and the response times; printing it shows the parameters at a bound and the event summary. parameters: path, value, lower, upper, scale, at_bound ("lower", "upper" or NA) and note, which says what a bound means where it switches part of the model off. A lower bound of zero is usually a natural value (no delay, no threshold) and is not flagged, except for a split recharge's recharge.alpha: at 0 every drop of direct runoff goes to groundwater and the surface stores carry nothing; at 1 none reaches groundwater. Events are taken one per flood (find_events(independent = TRUE)). events: every event with its period and the columns of event_scores(). summary: one row per window with events (the number summarised), median_peak_error, median_abs_peak_error (the median size of the peak errors, so that errors of -50% and +50% do not cancel), median_timing_error_h, share_peak_within_20pct and median_event_nse, and screened_out, the events of that window the screen left out. response_h: the response times estimated from the observed and the simulated flow.

Details

Parameters at a bound. A parameter that ends at the edge of its search range is usually being bent to make up for something the structure cannot do, not estimating a property of the catchment. Each parameter is checked against the widest range any calibration on the way to the entry searched it over, on a log scale where it was searched on one. A lower bound of zero, such as no time delay, is a natural limit rather than an imposed one, and is not flagged.

The largest events. Events are found with find_events() from the registered rain and observed flow and scored with event_scores(). In each window (calibration, validation, the held-back wettest years, and any outside them), the top largest by observed peak are summarised: median peak error, median timing error, the share of peaks within 20% of the observed, and median event NSE. Events are first screened with screen_events(); those it leaves out are kept in events with their flags, but not summarised.

See also

find_events(), event_scores(), pdm_stages()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
checks <- calibration_checks("projects/beggearn_huish")
checks$parameters[!is.na(checks$parameters$at_bound), ]
checks$summary
} # }
